:::{#exr-null-space-subspace-practice}
#### Showing that the solutions of two equations are a subspace

@thm-null-space-subspace turns a question about a [subspace](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-subspace)
into a question about a [null space](#def-null-space).
Let $\mathcal{S}$ hold the [solutions](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-linear-system) $\vecf{x} \in \reals^3$ of the two equations
$x_1 + x_2 - x_3 = 0$ and $x_2 = 2 x_3$.

Show that $\mathcal{S}$ is a subspace of $\reals^3$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Write both equations as $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vzero_2$ for one $2 \times 3$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{A}$.

:::

:::
